The five concrete echo argument cases and a zero-dispatch counter are best represented by the required parametrized input/expected-outcome table; a generic gate would hide the actual schema distinctions.
A sequence diagram makes call/result ID pairing and the required ordering before the next model request explicit.

Spatial boundaries distinguish host credentials/graders from the disposable task mount and configured execution restrictions.
A symlink arrow across the workspace boundary shows why an apparently in-root parent path can authorize the wrong destination.
Parallel caller/child timelines expose the time between a timeout and confirmed process termination, plus the separate cleanup allowance.

This is an audit of already implemented path, network, process, and credential boundaries. Its allowed/denied case matrix with prohibited-effect assertions is the precise visual organization; a new architecture picture cannot establish the tested guarantees.

JSONL event examples and an ordered table of sequence, run ID, call ID, and status expose the identifiers directly. A pictorial event chain would repeat that order while obscuring the actual fields to implement.
A branching diagram distinguishes viewing immutable events from replaying decisions through tools in a fresh fixture under a new run ID.
Eight graders require reference-pass and no-op/broken-fail controls. The mandated task-by-control table directly exposes missing cases; a schematic graph would not help assess these concrete checks.

The student must produce an eight-row report linked to real traces and distinguish fake from live runs. Use their actual outcome/cost table rather than an invented chart or a repeated evaluator diagram.
The two execution boundaries and protected grader inputs are central: the host controls grading but never imports agent-modified code.
The reservation-before-dispatch branch and unknown-usage branch are easier to reason about as control flow than as an accounting list.

The substantive comparison is a conditions table distinguishing typed tools from the pinned baseline command interface. A table preserves exact common limits and differing prompts more clearly than an architecture picture that might imply one-variable control.

This tiny two-task systems pilot needs actual paired result tables and a trace-linked note; plotting invented successes or equal-height budget boxes would obscure unequal consumption and interface confounds.

Stable file ordering, exclusion policy, and truncation metadata are best checked against concrete listing outputs on empty, nested, and over-limit fixtures. A repository tree would not show those exact return-contract decisions.
A file-line map makes requested, returned, truncated, and never-requested ranges visibly different without inventing an observed failure.
Paired branches show the single changed selector, fixed evaluator conditions, and intermediate selected evidence that establishes activation.

The exercise explicitly asks the learner to build a timeline from their saved evidence, actions, and grades. A supplied causal story could pre-empt that analysis or imply that one restored-excerpt replay proves causality.

This session defines a versioned durable-state schema and before/after records; a field/provenance table and actual JSON examples expose missing reservations, IDs, budgets, and workspace versions more precisely than a schema tree. The temporal crash gap is visualized in 7-2.
A two-lane timeline shows the non-atomic gap between checkpoint intent, workspace mutation, and checkpoint completion.
The ordered after/before/conflict branches show when a replacement is skipped, safely retried, or stopped.

The fault hooks and write-count assertions must be inspected in the learner’s own before/after interruption traces. Repeating the 7-2 crash-window picture would not verify that their implementation avoids a second write or preserves its deadline.
At the first introduction of compaction, a durable-log versus bounded-input layout makes lossy selection distinct from deleting storage.
Two file snapshots with a versioned line-range pointer show why the same line numbers do not guarantee the same evidence after an edit.
Side-by-side requests under one ceiling make the compact-record versus recent-history allocation difference visible while preserving fixed content and complete groups.

The learner’s original and compacted payloads are the evidence for an exact omitted fact. A supplied loss example could be mistaken for a result or substitute for the required natural/injected diagnostic distinction.
Converging direct and MCP paths show that transport adds no authorization shortcut and that both paths share the host checks.
The installed SDK’s minimal client/server code and a deterministic smoke trace are clearer than a duplicate of 9-1’s shared permission topology; protocol APIs must match the pinned version.
Four identical input cases through two interfaces require a parity table retaining content and error categories. That direct mapping is more precise than another fork-and-merge diagram.

The task is to inspect the actual adapter call graph and prove denied requests cannot alter trusted configuration. Existing 9-1 explains the topology; the saved permitted/denied smoke trace is the evidence here.

Authoring the final four fixtures requires concrete requests, references, and grader contracts, not another split diagram. The sixteen-task manifest and model-free control rows are the useful organization.
Reference, no-op, and deliberately broken states are an exact task-by-control matrix. The required table and assertions make permissive graders visible without a generic branching picture.

A manifest record directly maps task IDs to fixture/grader hashes, split membership, and commit. The optional already-ready external branch is a short checklist; a graph would duplicate these fields and add little.
The exercise validates hashes, counts, and controls against rebuilt fixtures. Its audit table and explicit negative test cases reveal discrepancies better than an abstract identity graph.
Error classification and remaining-budget branches form a real retry loop; the diagram makes permanent stops and rechecking limits explicit.
A phase/branch diagram separates rejection before execution, a failure after entry, and cancellation cleanup, preventing a single unsafe retry category.
A summary coverage marker against later durable event sequence numbers shows staleness independently of timestamps.

A failure matrix is explicitly the best representation for execution state, classification, permitted recovery, and limits across all cases. The learner must fill it from real traces, not copy a generic recovery diagram.

The two-condition table must list exact pinned settings and a written hypothesis. The policy contents are already visualized in 8-3; another parallel diagram would not replace precise model, tool, ceiling, and overhead declarations.
At study planning, the task-by-condition-by-repeat grid explains six observations per task and the 96-row design without treating repeats as independent tasks.
An explicitly illustrative pre-selection/selected-size plot shows the threshold intervention the pilot must actually exercise and the input ceiling it must respect.
A development feedback loop ending at the freeze, followed by manifest validation and final trials, exposes the no-final-feedback rule.

This is operational execution of the first frozen repeat. The required 32-row status table and live trace paths show real running/terminal states; a schematic dashboard would neither teach a new mechanism nor establish the actual outcomes.
The second repeat must retain the first round’s failures and unchanged hashes. A cumulative status/usage table and version checks directly demonstrate that invariant; no new diagram is needed.

The lab already calls for a student-generated plot or comparison table from audited trial data, with denominators and units. Supplying a precomputed teaching result would be less useful and could be confused with the learner’s measurements.

Representative trace excerpts selected by a declared rule are the correct evidence. A generic causal diagram could overstate what one failure establishes or preselect the interpretation the learner must test.
The optional pilot gates are a short conjunctive checklist with an explicit skip path, followed by a real twenty-row results table. A flowchart adds no substantial structure to that decision.

A private-versus-external comparison table directly states task counts, repeat counts, environments, and denominators. That exact mapping explains why pooling changes weights more clearly than proportional blocks without actual outcomes.

Original grades, saved evidence, and audited corrections belong side by side in the required audit table. A schematic regrading flow would not validate task contracts and might obscure preserved originals.

Reservations, usage-derived estimates, and billed charges need a reconciliation table with currency, pricing date, credits, and unresolved differences. The control-flow role of reservations already has a diagram in 5-2.
A cluster layout shows all six records traveling together when a task ID is resampled, preserving pairing and task weighting.
The lesson turns audited numbers into scoped prose using a findings generator and assertions. Exact reported metrics and a limitations paragraph are clearer than a generic claims diagram.
